motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Selection, focus, and inline disclosure only.

narrative.overview: Omakeyd is a compact, theme-native Quattro instrument. One continuous hierarchy keeps the selected keyboard, effective layout, and mapping path legible before any change is applied.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous panel hierarchy, not a dashboard of cards.
State motion only, 120-180 ms, with no entrance choreography.
Device identity and mapping provenance are visible before commitment.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: A plugin that looks correct in only one Omarchy theme is incorrect.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Accent color identifies the current selection, focus, and the primary apply action. It is never decoration.

rules.name: The Two Names Rule
rules.body: Prefer the human label first, then the exact system identifier in quieter text.

rules.name: The Single Surface Rule
rules.body: Do not nest card surfaces inside the panel. Separators, spacing, and headers establish hierarchy.

dos: Do state the selected keyboard immediately above all layout actions.
Do distinguish effective physical layout from raw XKB keymap whenever keyd or firmware remapping is present.
Do reuse Quattro controls and dynamic theme tokens without private approximations.
donts: Don't build a global language flag that hides the target keyboard.
Don't build a settings dashboard made from nested cards.
Don't report raw XKB names as if they were always the effective physical layout.
Don't rewrite /etc/keyd or ask for a password on every switch.
Don't use decorative gamer styling, neon accents, glassmorphism, or animated keyboard theatrics.
